generatedProse.concept-context: A psychology discovery service search becomes precise when you control it. You join concepts with AND, group each concept's synonyms with OR, and hold phrases such as 'mental health' together with quotation marks. A wildcard on 'adolescen*' catches both adolescent and adolescents, and a date limiter keeps the results to recent work. These tools turn a flood of hits into a set you can actually read.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students take the same keyword set into the discovery service to search for work on social media and adolescents' sleep.

Tom types all the words in one after another, with spaces between them. The service returns tens of thousands of results, far too many to use, and he gives up on the later pages. The terms were there, but nothing told the service how they fit together.

Amara joins the terms with operators, grouping the synonyms with OR and the concepts with AND, and puts quotation marks around each phrase. The wildcards catch the word endings, and the result is a few hundred focused hits. A date limiter for the last five years makes the set manageable.

Both used the same keywords. Amara told the service how they fit together, then refined from there.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, a discovery service lets you control a search rather than just run it. You join concepts with AND, group synonyms with OR, hold phrases together with quotation marks, catch word endings with a wildcard, and narrow with limiters. When a search returns too much or too little, you refine it and run it again. You can now construct and refine a psychology search of your own.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do to cut tens of thousands of results down to a usable set?

items.text: She combined the terms with operators and phrases, then added a date limiter.
She read further into the later pages of results.
She removed the keywords and searched the topic name alone.
She searched the same words again in a different order.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara combined the terms with operators and phrases, then narrowed with a limiter.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the moves that told the service how the terms fit together and narrowed the set.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara used operators and phrases to combine the terms, then a date limiter to narrow. Reading on, dropping keywords or reordering would not focus the search.
